 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act',
for short) has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment dated 26.04.2017 passed by the 1st Senior NC: 2023:KHC:40606 Civil Judge & IV MACT at Chitradurga (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.951/2016.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 04.01.2016 at about 3.00 p.m.
the deceased Rangappa was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-14/J-5755 from Marenadu Palya to Hiriyur.

When they reached near Pillajanahalli gate SH 19, at that time, a Tata M E Parvathamma vs The Inspector Of Excise on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172291348/
2 Sumo CS van bearing registration No.KA-16/G-356 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the vehicle of the deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased fell down, sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. On service of summons, the respondent Nos.1 to 4 appeared through counsel and respondent Nos. 1, 3 and 4 have filed written statements in which the averments made in the petition were denied.
The age, NC: 2023:KHC:40606 occupation and income of the deceased are denied.
It was pleaded that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased himself.
It was further pleaded that the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant.
Hence, they sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove their case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
On behalf of respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R2.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia

, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.16,03,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed NC:
2023:KHC:40606 respondent Nos. 3 and 4 to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.
6. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
(i) Firstly, the claimants claim that at the time of the accident the deceased was an agriculturist and doing dairy business and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
But the Tribunal is not justified in taking the monthly income of the deceased as only Rs.8,000/-.

(ii) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the claimants are entitled for addition of 40% towards 'future prospects'.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he prays for allowing the appeal.
7. On the other hand, the learned AGA for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:

(i) Firstly, even though the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.50,000/- per month, the same is not established by the claimants by producing M E Parvathamma vs The Inspector Of Excise on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172291348/
3 documents.

entities.text: M E Parvathamma vs The Inspector Of Excise
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased notionally.
(ii) Secondly, since the claimants have not established the income of the deceased, they are not entitled for addition of future prospects.

(iii) Thirdly, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal for 'loss of consortium', 'loss of love and affection' and 'loss of guidance' is on the higher side contrary to the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM reported in 2018 ACJ 2782.

entities.text: MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM reported in 2018 ACJ 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) Fourthly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award and original records.
9. It is not in dispute that Rangappa died in the road traffic accident occurred on 04.01.2016 due to rash and negligent driving of the Tata Van bearing registration No.KA-16/G-356 by its driver.
10. The claimants have not produced any evidence or documents with regard to the income of the deceased.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2016, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.9,500/- p.m.
To the aforesaid amount, 40% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in PRANAY SETHI (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.13,300/-, out of which, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd towards personal expenses and therefore, the monthly income comes to Rs.8,867/-.
The deceased was NC: 2023:KHC:40606 aged about 30 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.
Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.18,08,868/- (Rs.8,867*12*17) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE (supra), the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of consortium'.
11.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 18,08,868 M E Parvathamma vs The Inspector Of Excise on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172291348/
4  Funeral expenses 15,000  Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of spousal consortium 40,000  Loss of Parental consortium 80,000  Total 19,58,868  NC: 2023:KHC:40606 12.

In view of the above, I pass the following order:
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The judgment of the claims Tribunal is modified.

The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.19,58,868/- in place of Rs.16,03,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

(iii) The Insurance Company - respondent Nos. 3 and 4 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment, excluding interest for the delayed period of 891 days in filing the appeal.
